title: Telemetry Gateway and Adaptive Pager Broker for Noise Deconfliction
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight Telemetry Gateway that normalizes traces, metrics, and logs into a unified signal envelope and an Adaptive Pager Broker that deconflicts noisy alerts. Goal: reduce oncall fatigue and false-positive pages during partial degradations while preserving SLO fidelity and fast routing for high-confidence outages. The gateway will provide contextual trace hooks to the runtime, perform signature-based de-duplication across pipelines, and emit a signal confidence score consumed by the Pager Broker. The broker will synthesize routing priority using SLO burn-rate, recent signal reliability, customer tier, and recent incident context, allowing dynamic suppression or escalation policies.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry Gateway deployed to staging and normalizes incoming traces/metrics/logs into unified 'signal' objects with a confidence score and meta fields (service, route, model, region).
Gateway handles 10k signals/sec in staging with <100ms p50 processing latency and <1s p99, and autoscaling hooks defined.
Trace hooks inserted in inference runtime for prefix/KV cache hot-paths to attach request metadata (customer_id, model_variant, route) to spans; validated via synthetic trace benchmarks.
Adaptive Pager Broker routes alerts to the oncall rotation based on composite priority and can suppress/aggregate alerts with low confidence for configurable quiet windows.
New latency and error dashboards show per-route SLO burn visualization, signal confidence histograms, and the top 5 contributing anomalies with trace links.
End-to-end tests simulate noisy downstream (duplicate error logs + partial latency spikes) and demonstrate 60% reduction in duplicate pages vs baseline.
Runbook and Console docs updated (runbooks/team playbooks) and a post-deploy checklist exists.
notes: Decision: use existing Kafka ingestion layer and add an intermediate lightweight stream processor (Flink/Materialize prototype) to compute signal envelopes rather than heavy rework of current pipeline.

Trade-off: signature dedupe at gateway reduces noise but risks masking correlated multi-service outages; mitigation is to keep an SLA-weighted threshold and escalate when aggregated SLO burn crosses high threshold.
We will reuse the existing SLO datastore for burn-rate inputs but maintain a short-lived cache in the broker for sub-minute decisions.
Scope: initial rollout limited to production services in us-west-2 and shared runtime pool; subsequent phases expand to all regions and Dedicated tenants.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha K.: Prototype for the signal envelope is working. Using a lightweight JSON envelope with fields: service, route, model_variant, region, metrics_summary, trace_ids, confidence_score (0-1). Perf seems fine at 2k/s on dev nodes.
2025-02-21 - Marisol O. (SRE): Add a safety valve that forces pages when aggregated burn-rate > 5% regardless of confidence score. Otherwise we risk missing real incidents.

2025-02-28 - Design review - Approved with changes: add per-customer mute rules, retention of raw events for 7 days for debugging, and a fallback path that forwards raw alerts to existing pager if gateway is unhealthy.
2025-03-03 - Liam C.: Started implementing broker policy engine; working on lightweight DSL for composing rules (conditions + actions). Open question: UI for Console to edit rules vs config-as-code.

2025-03-04 - QA: End-to-end smoke shows trace hooks injecting customer_id properly; discovered edge case where streaming responses without finalization emit zero metrics_summary — fixed by emitting interim heartbeat metric.
implementation_notes: Plan to implement gateway processing as a Flink job with a thin Rust shim for signature hashing to reduce GC impact.
Broker policy engine will include a TTL-based suppression map and an audit log for actions taken on alerts.
Integrations: Opsgenie/SMS/Slack routing already supported by existing oncall infra; broker will emit normalized events to that pipeline.
Data retention: retain unified signals for 7 days, raw events for 30 days in cold storage (S3), traced spans referenced by id.
